canonical.description: IMS database descriptions and program views: 1 DBD(s), 0 PSB(s). Byte offsets and lengths are computed under the assumptions in extras['ims']['layoutAssumptions']; PROCOPT access profiles are in extras['ims']['psbs'].

capability_limits.detail: An LCHILD with POINTER=INDX pairs the segment with an index database (the HIDAM primary index or a secondary index). The index database is a separate DBD; it is named in extras['ims']['lchildren'] and not modelled.

An XDFLD is a search field built from source fields for a secondary index, not segment data; it is listed with its SRCH / SUBSEQ / DDATA / NULLVAL in extras['ims']['secondaryIndexes'] and not modelled as a field.

A DBD declares only the fields IMS sequences and searches on; the segment's other bytes are described by the application's copybook. The record keeps the declared fields at their offsets, and the undescribed byte ranges are listed in extras['ims']['undescribed'].
A variable-length segment (BYTES=(max,min)) has a different length in each occurrence; the record is laid out at its maximum and the bounds are in extras['ims']['variableLength'].

layoutAssumptions: START and BYTES are 1-based byte positions and byte lengths within the segment's data as IMS presents it to the program; the offset reported is START − 1.
One byte per character (TYPE=C) in a single-byte EBCDIC or ASCII code page.

TYPE=P is packed decimal — two digits per byte with the sign in the last nibble, so BYTES=n holds 2n − 1 digits; TYPE=Z is zoned decimal, one digit per byte. The DBD declares no scale, so neither carries a decimal point.
TYPE=H is a 2-byte and TYPE=F a 4-byte signed binary integer; TYPE=X is uninterpreted bytes.
In a variable-length segment (BYTES=(max,min)) the first two bytes of each occurrence hold its length; START positions are taken as written, not shifted past that prefix.
Byte ranges no FIELD covers are segment data the DBD does not describe — IMS needs FIELD statements only for the sequence field and the fields programs search on.
A SENFLD's START is the field's position in the program's I/O area, not in the stored segment.
